title: Application Health Diagnostics
description: Use Application Insights health checks and diagnostics to identify and resolve application issues.

data.text: Application Insights provides several diagnostic tools to help you understand your application health: the failures blade, performance reports, dependency maps, and the Application Map. These tools help you quickly pinpoint root causes without needing to reproduce the issue.

terms.definition: A visual map of your application components and their health, showing dependencies and failure rates.
A dedicated view that surfaces exceptions, failed requests, and dependency failures.
Shows endpoint performance, including average duration and dependency breakdown.
Captures debug snapshots when exceptions occur, including local variable values.

data.text: The Application Map shows your application as a graph of nodes and edges. Each node represents a component (web app, API, database) and edges represent dependencies. Clicking on a node reveals its health metrics, and clicking an edge shows call latency and failure rates.

data.text: Snapshot Debugger automatically captures debug snapshots when exceptions occur in your production application. Each snapshot includes the full stack trace, local variables, and method parameters, giving you the same debugging experience as local development.

data.title: Snapshot Debugger Prerequisites
data.text: Snapshot Debugger requires .NET Framework 4.6.1+, .NET Core 2.1+, or .NET 5+. The application must run with full trust. It is not available for Linux containers by default.

data.title: Diagnose a Production Exception
data.description: Use Application Map and Failures blade to investigate a failing endpoint.
steps: Open Application Map and identify the component with the lowest success rate.
Click on the component and view its most common exceptions.
Navigate to the Failures blade and group exceptions by type.
If using .NET, enable Snapshot Debugger and trigger the exception to capture a snapshot.
data.expectedOutcome: You have identified the failing component, its exception type, and (if applicable) a snapshot with variable values.
